title.en: Imperatives: Sit down! Don't run! Let's go!
title.sl: Velelnik: Sit down! Don't run! Let's go!
title.de: Der Imperativ: Sit down! Don't run! Let's go!
title.it: L'imperativo: Sit down! Don't run! Let's go!

rule.sl:
Ko komu rečeš, kaj naj naredi, vzameš osnovno obliko glagola, brez **you**: **Sit down!** (Sedi, sedite) **Shut the gate.** (Zapri vrata.) Oblika je ena sama: za eno osebo, za več ljudi in za vikanje. Slovenščina tu loči *sedi* in *sedite*, angleščina ne.

Za prepoved: **Don't** + osnovna oblika: **Don't run!** (Ne teci!) **Don't be late!** (Ne zamudi!) Nikoli *Not run!*, nikoli *Don't runs!* Na napisih je daljše **Do not**: **Do not feed the horses.**

Tudi **be** gre tako: **Be quiet!** (Bodi tiho!) **Be careful!** (Pazi!)

Za vse skupaj, tudi zase: **Let's** + osnovna oblika: **Let's go!** (Pojdimo!) **Let's have a cup of tea.** Nikoli *Let's to go*, nikoli *Let's going*. Za ne: **Let's not wait.** (Ne čakajmo.)

**please** (prosim) naredi stavek prijaznejši, na začetku ali na koncu: **Please come in.** **Come in, please.** Neznanca raje vprašaš: **Could you shut the door, please?**

Velelnik je tudi v navodilih, receptih in na napisih: **Turn left at the church.** (Pri cerkvi zavij levo.) **Stir the soup.** (Premešaj juho.) **Mind the step!** (Pazi na stopnico!) **Always** in **never** gresta na začetek: **Always shut the gate.** **Never leave the gate open.**
rule.de:
Wenn du jemandem sagst, was zu tun ist, nimmst du die Grundform des Verbs, ohne **you**: **Sit down!** (Setz dich, setzt euch, setzen Sie sich) **Shut the gate.** (Mach das Gatter zu.) Eine Form für alle: eine Person, mehrere, Fremde.

Für ein Verbot: **Don't** + Grundform: **Don't run!** (Lauf nicht!) **Don't be late!** (Komm nicht zu spät!) Nie *Not run!*, nie *Don't runs!* Auf Schildern steht die lange Form **Do not**: **Do not feed the horses.**

**be** geht genauso: **Be quiet!** (Sei still!) **Be careful!** (Pass auf!)

Für euch alle, dich eingeschlossen: **Let's** + Grundform: **Let's go!** (Gehen wir!) **Let's have a cup of tea.** Nie *Let's to go*, nie *Let's going*. Verneint: **Let's not wait.** (Warten wir nicht.)

**please** (bitte) macht es freundlicher, vorn oder hinten: **Please come in.** **Come in, please.** Fremde fragst du besser: **Could you shut the door, please?**

Auch Wegbeschreibungen, Rezepte und Schilder sagen es so: **Turn left at the church.** (Bieg bei der Kirche links ab.) **Stir the soup.** (Rühr die Suppe um.) **Mind the step!** (Achtung, Stufe!) **Always** und **never** kommen nach vorn: **Always shut the gate.** **Never leave the gate open.**
rule.it:
Per dire a qualcuno che cosa fare usi la forma base del verbo, senza **you**: **Sit down!** (Siediti, sedetevi, si sieda) **Shut the gate.** (Chiudi il cancello.) Una forma per tutti: una persona, tante, chi dai del Lei.

Per vietare: **Don't** + forma base: **Don't run!** (Non correre!) **Don't be late!** (Non fare tardi!) Mai *Not run!*, mai *Don't runs!* Sui cartelli c'è la forma lunga **Do not**: **Do not feed the horses.**

Anche **be** funziona così: **Be quiet!** (Fai silenzio!) **Be careful!** (Fai attenzione!)

Per tutti voi, tu compreso: **Let's** + forma base: **Let's go!** (Andiamo!) **Let's have a cup of tea.** Mai *Let's to go*, mai *Let's going*. Al negativo: **Let's not wait.** (Non aspettiamo.)

**please** (per favore) è più gentile, all'inizio o alla fine: **Please come in.** **Come in, please.** A uno sconosciuto è meglio chiedere: **Could you shut the door, please?**

Anche indicazioni, ricette e cartelli parlano così: **Turn left at the church.** (Alla chiesa gira a sinistra.) **Stir the soup.** (Mescola la minestra.) **Mind the step!** (Attenzione al gradino!) **Always** e **never** vanno all'inizio: **Always shut the gate.** **Never leave the gate open.**
rule.en:
To tell someone what to do, use the base form of the verb, with no **you**: **Sit down!** **Shut the gate.** It is one form for one person, for many and for a stranger.

For no: **Don't** + the base form: **Don't run!** **Don't be late!** Never *Not run!*, never *Don't runs!* Signs have the long form, **Do not**: **Do not feed the horses.**

**be** works the same: **Be quiet!** **Be careful!**

For you and the others together: **Let's** + the base form: **Let's go!** **Let's have a cup of tea.** Never *Let's to go*, never *Let's going*. For no: **Let's not wait.**

**please** makes it friendly, first or last: **Please come in.** **Come in, please.** With a stranger, ask: **Could you shut the door, please?**

Directions, recipes and signs say it this way too: **Turn left at the church.** **Stir the soup.** **Mind the step!** **Always** and **never** go first: **Always shut the gate.** **Never leave the gate open.**
